# Databases for Automation (SQL Basics and Storing Data)

## Overview
As your automations grow, storing data in spreadsheets stops being enough, and knowing basic databases makes you far more capable and credible. Spreadsheets are great for small, simple data, but they slow down with volume, struggle with reliable lookups and relationships, and can be corrupted by concurrent writes. A real database solves this: it stores data in tables (rows and columns, like a spreadsheet but far more robust), enforces structure, handles large volumes, and supports fast, precise queries even with millions of records. The universal language for talking to relational databases is SQL, and you only need the four core operations to be productive: SELECT reads data (SELECT email FROM customers WHERE status = 'active'), INSERT adds new rows, UPDATE modifies existing rows, and DELETE removes them. These map neatly onto what your automations already do - log a record (INSERT), find a customer (SELECT), change a status (UPDATE) - so SQL simply gives you a more powerful, reliable backend than a sheet. All three platforms can connect to databases: n8n and Make have Postgres/MySQL nodes, and you can also call a database through its API. For beginners, hosted database services make this painless - Supabase gives you a free Postgres database with a friendly interface and an auto-generated API, and Airtable (from Day 16) bridges the spreadsheet-to-database gap. Learning when to graduate from a sheet to a proper database, and being able to write basic SQL to store and retrieve your automation's data, signals real engineering maturity and is frequently expected in automation roles.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: When a spreadsheet is not enough; Relational databases and tables; Basic SQL: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE; Connecting databases (PostgreSQL/MySQL) to n8n/Make; Hosted databases (Supabase, Airtable) for beginners. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
Practical Task: Set up a free hosted database (Supabase), create a table, and from an automation (n8n/Make) or a Python script INSERT a new record and then SELECT it back to confirm it stored correctly.
Mini Project: Replace a spreadsheet backend with a database: create a table for leads/orders, update an existing automation to INSERT new records and UPDATE their status, and add a SELECT-based lookup step to prevent duplicates.
Assignment: Write the four core SQL statements for a 'customers' table with example values, and explain three specific problems a database solves that a spreadsheet does not.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.

## Next Steps After Today
- Complete the practical task and submit it for AI review.
- Read any research papers linked for deeper theory.
- Prepare questions for tomorrow's module.

## Resources
- Use the linked videos and documentation as reference material.
- Read the research papers for theoretical depth.
- Check the GitHub repositories for working code examples.
